## Summary

Define Relation

## Claim

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
# model
Relation;

Relation.** {:1}((IS_PROPERTY_OF)) (Relation, Relation.**);
(Relation, Relation.**) {:0+}((HAS_PROPERTY)) Relation.**;

# instances
Relation//$relation;
$relation.** {:1}((IS_PROPERTY_OF)) ($relation, $relation.**);
($relation, $relation.**) {:0+}((HAS_PROPERTY)) $relation.**;
```

### Prose Claim

Relation defines a reusable directed graph Relation Type with a Name and Meaning. Each actual link is a tuple (Host, Relation Type, Target); persist each direct fact once. An actual edge does not create a separate Relation ID. Endpoints are declared model Entities or instances, including Carrier and CFEL descriptors, and exclude literal values and glyphs. An operator is distinct from a graph Relation even when its notation spells a Relation traversal. Its declared descriptor may be an endpoint.

A direct Relation Declaration owns shared meaning, endpoint signature and any counterpart binding. A derived counterpart remains a distinct Relation with its own Declaration; its meaning and endpoints are inferred through that binding. An alias supplies lexical notation for one Relation; it does not create a new Relation, a Node or a separate Relation ID.

## Summary

Define Term

## Claim

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
# model
Term.*[in (Name)]{:1}
```

### Prose Claim

A Term is a reusable word or phrase component of entity expressions and authored content. Its Project-specific meaning remains consistent across uses and is owned by its active Method/Form Term Definition. Vocabulary Terms are lexical items, not graph Nodes merely because they are used as words. A Term has one Name.

Use the full admitted canonical expression when identifying or comparing an entity. Reusing a Term within distinct expressions neither makes those expressions synonymous nor establishes a Relation between their referents. Literal source quotations and code identifiers are not automatically renamed. A lexical Term and an Entity whose complete name uses that Term have distinct targets and meaning owners.

## Semantics

A Term provides a reusable word or phrase; its full context supplies the expression in which it appears.
